subject: Chemistry
name: Theory (Core)
description: Core theory covering structure and bonding, elements in the body and Group I metals, aluminium extraction, organic chemistry and chromatography, carbon and chromium compounds, sulfur dioxide and rates, iron and rusting, and organic homologous series.

parts.label: a(i)
parts.question: Fig. 1.1 shows seven structures A–G: A (giant ionic Na⁺Br⁻ lattice), B (giant covalent diamond-like C), C (simple molecular H₂O bent), D (simple molecular CO₂ linear), E (giant metallic Zn lattice), F (alloy Cu/Zn mixed lattice), G (simple molecular CH₄ tetrahedral). State which structure represents an alloy.

parts.label: a(ii)
parts.question: State which structure represents a substance that only conducts electricity when molten or in aqueous solution.

parts.label: a(iii)
parts.question: State which structure represents a giant covalent structure.

parts.label: a(iv)
parts.question: State which structure represents a compound that is a product formed in a hydrogen–oxygen fuel cell.

parts.label: a(v)
parts.question: State which structure represents a compound with a high melting point.

parts.label: a(vi)
parts.question: State which structure represents a gas that is responsible for increased global warming.

parts.label: b
parts.question: Complete Fig. 1.2 to show the dot-and-cross diagram for structure C (water, H₂O). Show outer shell electrons only. O has 6 outer electrons, each H has 1; two O-H bonds and two lone pairs on O.

questions.topic: Elements in the Body & Group I Metals

parts.label: a(i)
parts.question: Table 2.1 shows percentages by mass of elements in the human body: Ca 1.50, C 18.00, Cl 0.15, H 10.00, Mg 0.05, N 3.00, O 65.00, P 1.00, K 0.35, Na 0.15, S 0.25, other 0.55. Name the non-metallic element that has the lowest percentage by mass.

parts.label: a(ii)
parts.question: Name an element in Table 2.1 that is in Period 4 of the Periodic Table.

parts.label: b
parts.question: Some medicines contain a compound made of Mg²⁺ ions and OH⁻ ions. Name the compound made of Mg²⁺ ions and OH⁻ ions.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Describe the observations when aqueous sodium hydroxide is added dropwise to a solution containing calcium ions until the sodium hydroxide is in excess.

parts.label: d
parts.question: Name a calcium salt that is soluble in water.

parts.label: e
parts.question: Table 2.2 shows Group I metal properties: Li (mp 181°C), Na (mp 98°C, bubbles rapidly, no flame), K (bubbles very rapidly and flame), Rb (mp 39°C, explodes). Predict the melting point of potassium and the observations when lithium reacts with water.

parts.label: f
parts.question: State how the density of the Group I elements changes down the group.

parts.label: g
parts.question: Sodium reacts with water to produce sodium hydroxide and a gas which pops with a lighted splint. Complete the symbol equation: .....Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + ......

parts.label: a
parts.question: Aluminium is extracted by electrolysis of its purified ore. Name the main ore of aluminium.

parts.label: b(i)
parts.question: Fig. 3.1 shows the apparatus used in the extraction of aluminium (electrolytic cell with + and – power supply, steel case). Label the cathode in the diagram.

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.question: The electrolyte contains molten aluminium oxide. State the product formed at each electrode.

parts.label: c
parts.question: State two physical properties that explain why aluminium is used in overhead electrical cables.

parts.label: d(i)
parts.question: Sodium hydroxide is an alkali. State the meaning of the term alkali.

parts.label: d(ii)
parts.question: Describe how to find the pH of a dilute solution of sodium hydroxide using universal indicator paper.

parts.label: d(iii)
parts.question: A dilute solution of sodium hydroxide is added to a solution of methyl orange in acid until the sodium hydroxide is in excess. State the colour change of the methyl orange.
keywords: methyl orange in acid is red
methyl orange in alkali is yellow

parts.label: a
parts.question: Fig. 4.1 shows the displayed formula of a compound extracted from a plant (a large molecule with C=C double bonds). On the diagram, draw a circle around one functional group that makes this compound unsaturated.

parts.label: b(i)
parts.question: Fig. 4.2 shows results of chromatography of coloured compounds from four plants Q, R, S and T on filter paper with solvent front marked. Deduce which plant contains the greatest number of coloured compounds.

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.question: Deduce which two plants contain exactly the same coloured compounds (look for identical spot patterns).

parts.label: b(iii)
parts.question: State the meaning of the term solvent.

parts.label: c(i)
parts.question: Plants produce glucose and oxygen by photosynthesis. Complete the word equation: ........................ + ........................ → glucose + oxygen

parts.label: c(ii)
parts.question: Name one other substance that is essential for photosynthesis.

parts.label: a
parts.question: An atom of carbon is represented by ¹⁴C (atomic number 6, mass number 14). Describe this atom in terms of: the position of electrons, neutrons and protons; the number of neutrons and protons; and the electronic configuration.

parts.label: b(i)
parts.question: Complete the symbol equation for the incomplete combustion of carbon to produce carbon monoxide. .....C + O₂ → .....CO

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.question: State one adverse effect of carbon monoxide.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Fig. 5.1 shows the displayed formula of chromium carbonyl (Cr atom surrounded by 6 CO groups bonded through carbon). Deduce the molecular formula of chromium carbonyl.

parts.label: d
parts.question: Another chromium compound has formula Na₂Cr₂C₁₀O₁₀. Complete Table 5.1 to calculate Mr. Na: 2×23=46, Cr: 2×52=104, C: 10×12=120, O: 10×16=160. Find Mr.

parts.label: e
parts.question: Chromium can be produced by heating chromium(III) oxide with carbon: Cr₂O₃ + 3C → 2Cr + 3CO. Describe how this equation shows that chromium(III) oxide is reduced.

parts.label: a
parts.question: Large pieces of solid sulfur burn in excess oxygen to produce sulfur dioxide gas. Complete the equation by adding the missing state symbol: S(.....) + O₂(g) → SO₂(g)

parts.label: b
parts.question: Fig. 6.1 shows how the mass of sulfur changes with time as it burns (graph: mass decreases from ~32g to 0g, levelling off at about 80s). Deduce the time taken for the reaction to finish.

parts.label: c
parts.question: The experiment is repeated using powdered sulfur. Describe the effect on the rate of reaction of using powdered sulfur rather than large pieces of sulfur.

parts.label: d(i)
parts.question: Sulfur dioxide reacts with oxygen: 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇋ 2SO₃(g). Describe the effect on the rate: (1) temperature is decreased; (2) pressure of gases is increased. All other conditions stay the same.

parts.label: d(ii)
parts.question: Changing concentration changes the rate of a reaction. Choose the correct unit of concentration from the list. Circle your answer.

parts.label: e(i)
parts.question: Sulfur dioxide is an air pollutant. State one adverse effect of sulfur dioxide.

parts.label: e(ii)
parts.question: Emissions of sulfur dioxide can be reduced by using low-sulfur fossil fuels. State one other way of reducing sulfur dioxide emissions from fossil fuels.

parts.label: f
parts.question: A sealed tube contains aqueous sodium hydrogen sulfite at the bottom releasing SO₂ gas. Filter paper soaked in acidified potassium manganate(VII) is attached at the top. The filter paper remains purple at first then becomes colourless after a short time. Explain these results in terms of kinetic particle theory.

parts.label: a
parts.question: Iron is a metal with high density, high melting point and high boiling point. State three other physical properties of iron.

parts.label: b(i)
parts.question: State the conditions needed for iron to rust.

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.question: Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide. State if iron(III) oxide is an acidic or basic oxide. Give a reason for your answer.

parts.label: b(iii)
parts.question: Complete this sentence about preventing rusting. Rusting can be prevented by painting or ........................................

parts.label: c
parts.question: Five metals: calcium, copper, iron, silver, sodium. Put these metals in order of reactivity, most reactive at the top.

parts.label: d
parts.question: Complete the word equation for the reaction of calcium carbonate with nitric acid. calcium carbonate + nitric acid → ........................ + water + ........................

parts.label: a(i)
parts.question: Fig. 8.1 shows displayed formulae of five organic compounds V–Z: V (C₂H₆, alkane), W (C₂H₄, alkene), X (CH₃COOH, carboxylic acid), Y (C₂H₅OH, alcohol), Z (C₃H₇OH, alcohol). State which two compounds are in the same homologous series.

parts.label: a(ii)
parts.question: Explain why compound V (C₂H₆, ethane) is an alkane.

parts.label: a(iii)
parts.question: State the name of the homologous series to which compound X (CH₃COOH) belongs.

parts.label: b(i)
parts.question: Ethanol can be manufactured by the catalytic addition of steam to ethene. State the temperature and pressure required for this reaction.

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.question: Name one other method of manufacturing ethanol.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Describe how alkenes are manufactured from petroleum fractions.
